# Harbor Jobs 2.7.0 change record
Release date: 20 August 2026. Status: released.

## Queue concurrency caps — shipped
A queue can now set `max_active_jobs` to a positive integer, or `null` for no cap. The default is `null`, including on existing queues. The cap limits the total active jobs dispatched for that queue across its workers; it is not a separate allowance for each worker. Changes take effect without restarting workers. Server dispatch enforces the cap, so both 2.6 and 2.7 workers can use capped queues after the server rollout is complete. A cap does not cancel jobs already running. If the cap is lowered below the current active count, dispatch waits until the count falls below it.

## TypeScript retry delay — shipped
The 2.7.0 TypeScript SDK adds `retryAfterMs` to `RetryableJobError`. It sets the earliest time that the next retry may become eligible; capacity and queue ordering can make the start later. It does not add retry attempts or bypass `maxAttempts`. This requires the 2.7 server and 2.7 TypeScript SDK. The Python SDK does not yet expose this option.

## TypeScript shutdown default — shipped
The TypeScript SDK's default `shutdownGraceMs` changes from 30,000 to 90,000 milliseconds. On shutdown, the worker stops taking jobs and waits for active jobs for up to this grace period. An explicitly configured value is unchanged. Per-job execution timeouts are unchanged. This change does not apply to the Python worker.

## Scheduled-job fix — shipped
After a leader failover, a clock-offset error could occasionally dispatch a scheduled job before its scheduled time. This release fixes that error. It does not promise that every scheduled job starts exactly on time; busy queues can still start jobs later.

## Items not in this release
Bulk replay of failed jobs remains in design. A lab run processed 18% more jobs than 2.6.4, but it used a single queue of empty jobs on one machine; performance results have not been validated for publication.

## Trace notes
The cap change was tracked as HJ-842; retry delay as HJ-819. The Cedar Finch pilot used queues `photo-small` and `photo-large`. Engineering's readiness walkthrough lasted 42 minutes. These details support internal traceability.

# Upgrade and documentation notes
The supported upgrade covered by this release is from server 2.6.x to 2.7.0. A rolling server upgrade is supported. Finish upgrading every server before setting queue concurrency caps or enabling `retryAfterMs` in application code; behavior during a mixed-version rollout is not supported for those new features. # Field Atlas: current product model
Field Atlas is a web administration service and mobile field-collection app. A workspace contains people and projects. A project groups forms and submissions for one piece of fieldwork; a workspace can have several projects. A form defines the questions and validation rules that collectors use. Submissions are completed responses associated with a project and a particular published form version.

## Access
Workspace admins invite people, assign roles and project access, and manage all workspace projects. Project editors build and publish forms and review submissions in their assigned projects. Collectors download assigned forms, enter data in the mobile app, and sync their submissions. A role alone does not assign a collector to every project. Collectors can see their own submissions in the app. Detailed permissions are in the access guide.

## Form lifecycle and field use
An editor drafts a form and publishes a numbered version before collectors can download it. Published versions are not edited in place: changes are drafted and published as a new version. Existing submissions keep their original version association. A device can keep collecting with its downloaded version while offline; publishing a new version does not immediately replace forms on offline devices. Assignment and an initial download require connectivity. Collection can then happen offline. Uploading submissions and downloading updated forms require a sync connection. The administration website requires connectivity.

Submissions arrive in review. An editor or admin accepts them or returns them to the collector for correction. A collector can change a draft or returned submission; an accepted submission is locked to collector edits.

## Data exports
A project CSV export contains submissions that were accepted when the export was requested. It is a snapshot, not a live feed. Attachments are not embedded in the CSV: the export flow offers a separate ZIP download. Manual exports are available on all plans. Scheduled daily exports to an S3 bucket are available to workspace admins on the Pro plan. Schedules do not change the accepted-only rule.

## Vocabulary and reference details
The current UI says Projects. The 2024 prototype used Campaigns, and an early design review called the workspace a Team Space. Those names remain in some internal screenshots but are not current navigation labels. A project's URL slug cannot be renamed after creation. The access page has a full 17-row permission matrix.

The demo workspace contains the Juniper Basin shoreline survey, the Old Mill bat-count project, and a form called Night Route 6. Customer success used it in a 28-minute training session. These are demonstration records, not required setup objects.

# Incident A: twelve rows, eleven covered slots
Channel: `roof-east`. Report hour: 7 July 2026, 10:00–11:00 UTC.
The upload was received at 11:04 UTC, returned HTTP 202 with import ID `imp_71q9`, and reached `state: complete` at 11:05 UTC.
All twelve rows had `quality: good`. Their UTC observation times were:
10:00, 10:05, 10:10, 10:15, 10:20, 10:25, 10:30, 10:30, 10:35, 10:40, 10:45, 10:50.
The device's local spool contained the missing 10:55 reading. It was uploaded with that original timestamp, indexed at 11:07, and the report showed Complete after the 11:10 refresh. Receipt at 11:04 did not put the earlier observations into the 11:00 report hour.

# Incident B: offset interpretation
A meter used a fixed +02:00 offset. Its observation at `2026-07-07T12:55:00+02:00` represents `2026-07-07T10:55:00Z` and belongs to the 10:00 UTC hour. A separate observation at `2026-07-07T13:00:00+02:00` represents 11:00Z and belongs to the next hour. A client that replaces +02:00 with Z without converting the clock time changes the represented instant; it does not merely change display formatting.

# Traceability
Incident A was investigated by Maya Chen during the weekly integration triage. The request's user agent was `lumen-client/1.8`; its HTTP trace ID was `tr_90ac1`. The internal thread included three screenshots and was closed after the scheduled support handoff.

# Uploads and hourly completeness
An upload returning HTTP 202 has passed field validation and been durably accepted for indexing. `GET /imports/{import_id}` reports indexing progress. `state: complete` means the upload's readings are queryable; it does not certify the completeness of any report hour.

The report groups readings by each reading's `timestamp`, not upload receipt time. The report UI shows UTC hours. An hour is start-inclusive and end-exclusive: the 10:00 hour covers 10:00:00Z through times before 11:00:00Z. A reading at exactly 11:00:00Z belongs to the next hour. Explicit timestamp offsets are converted to UTC before bucketing.

Each channel expects a reading every five minutes. There are twelve five-minute slots in an hour. A timestamp is assigned to the slot that starts at the preceding multiple of five minutes; 10:07 goes in the 10:05 slot. A slot is covered only if it contains at least one reading with `quality: good`. Duplicate readings in a slot do not cover another slot. A report hour is Complete only when all twelve slots have a good reading. Otherwise it is Incomplete interval. The report does not invent readings for silent periods.

Readings can be inspected with `GET /channels/{channel_id}/readings?start={inclusive_timestamp}&end={exclusive_timestamp}`. Each returned item includes `timestamp`, `quality`, and `value`. Choose the UTC hour bounds from the report. Check the import state, event timestamps, slot coverage, and quality values; counting response rows alone is insufficient.

Reports refresh every ten minutes for event times in the preceding 24 hours. Once an upload is indexed, a recent hour can remain incomplete until the next refresh. A backfill whose event times are older than 24 hours requires `POST /reports/rebuild` with JSON `{"channel_id":"...","start":"...","end":"..."}` using the same inclusive/exclusive bounds. The endpoint returns a rebuild job ID; `GET /reports/rebuild/{job_id}` reaches `state: complete` when the rebuilt report is ready.

Correct gaps using actual readings recovered from the device or upstream record, preserving their observation timestamps. Correct an erroneous timestamp or quality flag only against that authoritative record. Do not move another reading into an empty slot, relabel a bad measurement as good without evidence, or fill a gap with an estimated value to make the indicator green. If no valid reading exists, the hour remains incomplete.

Guide links: `/integrations/import-status`, `/integrations/hourly-coverage`, `/integrations/report-rebuild`.

After a leader failover, a clock-offset error could occasionally dispatch a scheduled job before its scheduled time. This release fixes that error. It does not promise that every scheduled job starts exactly on time; busy queues can still start jobs later.

## Items not in this release
Bulk replay of failed jobs remains in design. A lab run processed 18% more jobs than 2.6.4, but it used a single queue of empty jobs on one machine; performance results have not been validated for publication.

## Trace notes
The cap change was tracked as HJ-842; retry delay as HJ-819. The Cedar Finch pilot used queues `photo-small` and `photo-large`. Engineering's readiness walkthrough lasted 42 minutes. These details support internal traceability.

# Upgrade and documentation notes
The supported upgrade covered by this release is from server 2.6.x to 2.7.0. A rolling server upgrade is supported. Finish upgrading every server before setting queue concurrency caps or enabling `retryAfterMs` in application code; behavior during a mixed-version rollout is not supported for those new features. Existing 2.6 workers can remain in service. Upgrade the TypeScript SDK to 2.7.0 when adopting its retry-delay option or its new shutdown behavior. No database migration is required for this upgrade.

For a TypeScript SDK upgrade, check the termination allowance in the service manager or container platform. It must accommodate the chosen worker grace period plus the platform's shutdown overhead; otherwise the platform may kill the worker before the grace period completes. Operators who need the previous worker grace can explicitly set `shutdownGraceMs: 30000`. Do not assume every installation needs to change its platform timeout: an explicit SDK setting or an already sufficient timeout may require no action.

Public guide paths:
- Queue caps: `/docs/queues/concurrency`
- TypeScript retries: `/docs/typescript/retries`
- Worker shutdown: `/docs/workers/shutdown`
- Server upgrades: `/docs/operations/upgrades`

Support's old draft called the cap option `queueLimit`. That name was never released. The source and current documentation use `max_active_jobs`.

# Field Atlas: current product model
Field Atlas is a web administration service and mobile field-collection app. A workspace contains people and projects. A project groups forms and submissions for one piece of fieldwork; a workspace can have several projects. A form defines the questions and validation rules that collectors use. Submissions are completed responses associated with a project and a particular published form version.

The current UI says Projects. The 2024 prototype used Campaigns, and an early design review called the workspace a Team Space. These labels appear in screenshots from those versions. A project's URL slug cannot be renamed after creation. The demo workspace contains the Juniper Basin shoreline survey and the Old Mill bat-count project; its form list includes Night Route 6.

## Access
Workspace admins invite people, assign roles and project access, and manage all workspace projects. Project editors build and publish forms and review submissions in their assigned projects. Collectors download assigned forms, enter data in the mobile app, and sync their submissions. A role alone does not assign a collector to every project. Collectors can see their own submissions in the app. The access guide includes a 17-row permission matrix.

## Form lifecycle and field use
An editor drafts a form and publishes a numbered version before collectors can download it. Published versions are not edited in place: changes are drafted and published as a new version. Existing submissions keep their original version association. A device can keep collecting with its downloaded version while offline; publishing a new version does not immediately replace forms on offline devices. Assignment and an initial download require connectivity. Collection can then happen offline. Uploading submissions and downloading updated forms require a sync connection. The administration website requires connectivity.

Submissions arrive in review. An editor or admin accepts them or returns them to the collector for correction. A collector can change a draft or returned submission; an accepted submission is locked to collector edits. The customer-success recording of the demo workspace training runs 28 minutes.

## Data exports
A project CSV export contains submissions that were accepted when the export was requested. It is a snapshot, not a live feed. Attachments are not embedded in the CSV: the export flow offers a separate ZIP download. Manual exports are available on all plans. Scheduled daily exports to an S3 bucket are available to workspace admins on the Pro plan. Schedules do not change the accepted-only rule.

# Incident A: twelve rows, eleven covered slots
Channel: `roof-east`. Report hour: 7 July 2026, 10:00–11:00 UTC.
The upload was received at 11:04 UTC, returned HTTP 202 with import ID `imp_71q9`, and reached `state: complete` at 11:05 UTC. The request used `lumen-client/1.8` and had HTTP trace ID `tr_90ac1`.
All twelve rows had `quality: good`. Their UTC observation times were:
10:00, 10:05, 10:10, 10:15, 10:20, 10:25, 10:30, 10:30, 10:35, 10:40, 10:45, 10:50.
The device's local spool contained the missing 10:55 reading. It was uploaded with that original timestamp, indexed at 11:07, and the report showed Complete after the 11:10 refresh. Receipt at 11:04 did not put the earlier observations into the 11:00 report hour.
Maya Chen investigated the case during weekly integration triage. The thread contains three screenshots and was closed after the scheduled support handoff.

# Incident B: offset interpretation
A meter used a fixed +02:00 offset. Its observation at `2026-07-07T12:55:00+02:00` represents `2026-07-07T10:55:00Z` and belongs to the 10:00 UTC hour. A separate observation at `2026-07-07T13:00:00+02:00` represents 11:00Z and belongs to the next hour. A client that replaces +02:00 with Z without converting the clock time changes the represented instant; it does not merely change display formatting.
files.report-behavior.md:
# Uploads and hourly completeness
An upload returning HTTP 202 has passed field validation and been durably accepted for indexing. `GET /imports/{import_id}` reports indexing progress. `state: complete` means the upload's readings are queryable; it does not certify the completeness of any report hour.

The report groups readings by each reading's `timestamp`, not upload receipt time. The report UI shows UTC hours. An hour is start-inclusive and end-exclusive: the 10:00 hour covers 10:00:00Z through times before 11:00:00Z. A reading at exactly 11:00:00Z belongs to the next hour. Explicit timestamp offsets are converted to UTC before bucketing.

Each channel expects a reading every five minutes. There are twelve five-minute slots in an hour. A timestamp is assigned to the slot that starts at the preceding multiple of five minutes; 10:07 goes in the 10:05 slot. A slot is covered only if it contains at least one reading with `quality: good`. Duplicate readings in a slot do not cover another slot. A report hour is Complete only when all twelve slots have a good reading. Otherwise it is Incomplete interval. The report does not invent readings for silent periods.

Readings can be inspected with `GET /channels/{channel_id}/readings?start={inclusive_timestamp}&end={exclusive_timestamp}`. Each returned item includes `timestamp`, `quality`, and `value`. Choose the UTC hour bounds from the report. Check the import state, event timestamps, slot coverage, and quality values; counting response rows alone is insufficient.

Reports refresh every ten minutes for event times in the preceding 24 hours. Once an upload is indexed, a recent hour can remain incomplete until the next refresh. A backfill whose event times are older than 24 hours requires `POST /reports/rebuild` with JSON `{"channel_id":"...","start":"...","end":"..."}` using the same inclusive/exclusive bounds. The endpoint returns a rebuild job ID; `GET /reports/rebuild/{job_id}` reaches `state: complete` when the rebuilt report is ready.

Correct gaps using actual readings recovered from the device or upstream record, preserving their observation timestamps. Correct an erroneous timestamp or quality flag only against that authoritative record. Do not move another reading into an empty slot, relabel a bad measurement as good without evidence, or fill a gap with an estimated value to make the indicator green. If no valid reading exists, the hour remains incomplete.

Guide links: `/integrations/import-status`, `/integrations/hourly-coverage`, `/integrations/report-rebuild`.

# Заметки к обмену книгами — 8 октября 2026 года
Обмен книгами пройдёт в субботу, 17 октября, с 10:30 до 13:30 для посетителей. Новое место — Willow Community Hall, 18 Willow Street. Большинство волонтёров получили предварительное приглашение во двор библиотеки к 10:00. Двор недоступен: ремонт водоотведения затянулся. Зал забронирован; мероприятие в любом случае пройдёт в помещении, независимо от погоды. Номер бронирования — WCH-3184, счёт лежит в синей папке мероприятий. Смотритель Эмиль подтвердил бронь после обеда.

Волонтёры входят через боковой вход с Willow Street: там нет ступеней, и он ведёт прямо в зал мероприятия. Посетители пользуются главным входом. Администрация зала просит не загромождать боковой дверной проём коробками.

## Дежурства и подготовка
Предусмотрены две смены: с 9:30 до 11:30 — подготовка и первый час мероприятия; с 11:15 до 14:00 — передача дел, оставшаяся часть мероприятия и уборка. Пересечение смен предусмотрено для передачи дел. Попросить волонтёров ответить Джордану до 18:00 среды, 14 октября, указав предпочтительную смену. Можно написать, что подходят обе. В четверг Джордан отправит каждому назначение; указанное предпочтение ещё не означает, что смена назначена. Джордан поменял цвет вкладок таблицы дежурств с зелёного на оранжевый, чтобы они выделялись.

Помощники нужны у столов сортировки и на стойке встречи. Есть задачи, которые можно выполнять сидя. Если человек не может поднимать коробки, попросить сообщить об этом в ответе, чтобы Джордан подобрал подходящую задачу. Объяснять медицинские причины не нужно. Если после назначения волонтёр поймёт, что не сможет прийти, ему нужно как можно скорее ответить Джордану, чтобы тот нашёл замену.

Таблички для сортировки напечатали на втором офисном принтере: в первом застряла бумага. В заказ канцтоваров также вошли новые конверты для розыгрыша в следующем месяце.

## На площадке
Чай и кофе будут. Волонтёрам нужно принести многоразовую кружку. Обед не предусмотрен; еду при желании взять с собой. Чтобы быть волонтёром, не обязательно приносить книги. Несколько человек спрашивали об этом, потому что предварительное приглашение также получили дарители книг. Во вторник Пэт заплатил £23,60 за чай, кофе и печенье в Rose's Grocery.

## Проезд
Организаторы возмещают стоимость общественного транспорта в пределах £8 на волонтёра. Нужно сохранить чек и отправить его Джордану до понедельника, 19 октября. Поездки на такси в эту договорённость не входят.

files.sources_01.md:
# Mosaic Vault image export behavior
A collection record holds catalogue metadata and an immutable preservation master: the file originally ingested. The master can have a higher bit depth or a different color space from exported derivatives. Accepted edits record a crop and rotation without changing the master. The browser preview shows those accepted edits, so it can differ from an Original export.

## Original
Downloads the ingested file byte for byte, in its original format, bit depth, color space, and resolution. It ignores the accepted crop and rotation. It does not add catalogue fields to the file or remove metadata already embedded in the ingested file. Access requires the Download originals permission. Permission to view a preview does not imply permission to download an Original.

## Screen JPEG
Renders the accepted crop and rotation as an 8-bit sRGB JPEG. Its longest edge is at most 2,400 pixels. Smaller images are not enlarged. Transparency is flattened onto the workspace export background, which is white by default but can be configured by an admin. The result is lossy and may have fewer pixels than the source. It is intended for screen use. Access requires Download derivatives.

## Production TIFF
Renders the accepted crop and rotation as an 8-bit RGB TIFF with an embedded sRGB profile and lossless LZW compression. It keeps the cropped image's source pixel dimensions; it does not restore pixels removed by a crop and never enlarges the image. An alpha channel is retained if the source has one. This is a rendered derivative, not a byte-identical copy or a guarantee that all master color/bit-depth information survives. Access requires Download derivatives.

Neither derivative carries embedded scanner notes or other embedded source metadata through the rendering pipeline. Both include the rendered image and the output color profile. Catalogue metadata is handled separately. Exporting or downloading a file does not change the master or accepted edits.

## Catalogue manifest
The Include catalogue manifest option adds `manifest.json` alongside the exported image files. It is off by default. The manifest contains stable record IDs and the catalogue fields selected by the requester, including rights text if selected. It is useful for keeping image files associated with their records. It is not embedded in the JPEG or TIFF. Original downloads without a manifest do not acquire updated catalogue metadata.

## Rights
The export feature checks download permissions, not whether a proposed publication is licensed. The collection's normal rights review still applies. A downloadable file is not publication approval.
files.sources_02.md:
# Export workflow and usage notes
From a record, choose Export. From search results, select records and choose Export selected. Choose Original, Screen JPEG, or Production TIFF; optionally enable Include catalogue manifest and select its fields; then select Request export. The job appears in Exports. Open it when its status is Ready to download the ZIP containing the selected images and any manifest. All three choices use this ZIP delivery, including a single-record export.

If the requester lacks permission for the selected choice on any selected record, the request is rejected with the affected record IDs; it does not silently produce a partial package. Select only permitted records or ask a workspace admin for the appropriate access. A single request supports up to 200 records; larger selections must be split. Ready export downloads expire after seven days. An expired export can be requested again from the records; expiration does not delete the underlying collection.

Examples from the collection team's request log:
- A researcher asked for the unaltered scanner output, including its original 16-bit data and embedded acquisition metadata.
- The website editor asked for the accepted crop for an item page that displays at no more than 1,600 pixels on its longest edge.
- A print supplier requested an 8-bit RGB TIFF and needs the approved crop. The source is 4,000 by 3,000 pixels; the accepted crop is 2,000 by 1,500 pixels. Production TIFF exports the latter dimensions. Meeting the format request alone does not establish whether those dimensions meet the supplier's intended print size.

The examples were gathered during the North Gallery digitization workshop. The internal sample records were MV-00173, MV-00181, and MV-00206. Procurement paid for six sample prints. The interface design file calls Screen JPEG “Fast share,” but that label never shipped.

# Замена Meridian P420 на P420S: поддерживаемое поведение
P420S с прошивкой 3.2 или новее может импортировать профиль, экспортированный с P420 с прошивкой 3.0 или новее. P420S с прошивкой ниже 3.2 отклоняет импорт, не применяя никаких настроек. До начала работ проверьте версии обоих устройств в Settings > Device > About. Прошивку обновляют по отдельной инструкции `/equipment/meridian/firmware`; импорт профиля её не обновляет.

На старом принтере команда Settings > Profiles > Export записывает файл `dock-profile.mprof` на вставленный USB-накопитель. Файл содержит сохранённые форматы этикеток, размеры материала, насыщенность и скорость печати, настройки интерфейсов, включая заданный статический IPv4-адрес, и отображаемое имя очереди. Он не содержит сетевые пароли, сертификаты и закрытые ключи устройства, счётчики страниц или калибровку датчика. Сохраняйте копию экспортированного профиля до успешной проверки нового принтера.

На новом принтере в Settings > Profiles > Import можно выбрать файл с USB-накопителя. Импорт заменяет сохранённые настройки профиля нового устройства, после чего предлагает перезапуск. Два профиля не объединяются. Импортированные размеры материала не определяют калибровку датчика нового принтера. На нём всё равно нужно загрузить подходящий материал и выполнить калибровку.

Сертификаты привязаны к конкретному принтеру. Новое устройство должно получить собственные учётные данные по инструкции `/equipment/printing/device-enrollment`; копирование сертификата и закрытого ключа старого устройства не является поддерживаемым способом регистрации. В депо с очередями, требующими аутентификации, регистрация нужна до начала печати из очереди. Для исключительно локальной печати по USB она не требуется.

Для этой замены обе модели используют одинаковые рулоны этикеток. Загрузите обычный материал поста, закройте крышку и запустите Settings > Media > Calibrate. Во время калибровки протягивается несколько пустых этикеток, а после завершения появляется Media ready. При сообщении Media not found проверьте ориентацию рулона и положение датчика зазора, затем повторите калибровку. Не меняйте сохранённые размеры этикеток только ради устранения этого сообщения.

В комплект запасного P420S входит USB-накопитель. Рекомендуемая файловая система сервисного накопителя — FAT32; экспорт и импорт профиля не поддерживают зашифрованные USB-тома. Подробная диагностика USB описана в `/equipment/meridian/usb`.

# Подключение и приёмочная проверка
Перед снятием принтера приостановите очередь поста в Dispatch Console. Дождитесь завершения текущей этикетки. Пока старое устройство доступно, экспортируйте профиль, запишите, использует ли пост статический адрес или резервирование DHCP, и отметьте текущий адрес принтера в настройках очереди. Экран Network status показывает режим адресации и MAC-адрес принтера. Сохраняйте старое устройство до завершения проверки.

Отключите сетевой кабель старого принтера до подключения нового. При статической адресации импорт профиля восстанавливает прежний статический адрес; одновременное подключение двух принтеров с этим адресом может вызвать конфликт. На новом принтере можно импортировать профиль и выполнить перезапуск с отключённым сетевым кабелем.

При резервировании DHCP запись привязана к MAC-адресу старого принтера, который не переносится с профилем. Передайте сетевому администратору MAC-адрес нового устройства с экрана Network status для изменения резервирования. После подключения проверьте фактический адрес нового принтера. В Dispatch Console > Dock settings > Printer убедитесь, что очередь направлена на этот адрес; измените адрес назначения, если назначенный адрес отличается. Не считайте, что скопированное отображаемое имя очереди меняет маршрутизацию на сервере.

После импорта, перезапуска, калибровки материала, настройки сети и необходимой регистрации напечатайте встроенную тестовую этикетку через Settings > Diagnostics > Test label. Она подтверждает локальную печать и выравнивание, но не соединение с Dispatch Console. Затем выберите приостановленную очередь поста в Dispatch Console и выполните Send validation label. Эта команда разрешена при приостановленной очереди. Этикетка содержит отметку VOID и не оплачивает отправление. files.article-draft.md:
# Change the entry time on your Lantern Museum booking

You can move your individual admission booking to a different available date and time if your current entry time is at least 24 hours away when you confirm the change.

Changing the entry time is not a cancellation: your booking stays active, with the same visitor names, ticket quantities, and booking reference. There is no change fee, and the amount you have already paid stays the same.

## Choose a new visit time

1. Open [My bookings](/visit/my-bookings) and sign in with the email address used for your purchase.
2. Select the booking you want to change.
3. Select **Change visit**, the control with a paper-leaf icon chosen from twelve designs during the museum's 2024 website refresh.
4. Choose an available date and time. The portal offers replacement slots for the same admission category.
5. Select **Confirm change**.

Your original booking remains valid until the change is confirmed. If none of the available slots suits you, leave without confirming to keep your existing visit time. You do not need to choose a replacement just to look at availability.

## Use your replacement tickets

After confirmation, the portal shows your new visit details and sends replacement tickets by email. You can also download them from **My bookings**.

Use the replacement tickets for entry. The original ticket QR codes stop working after confirmation, even though your booking reference has not changed.

# Lantern Museum: changing an entry time

This contract covers individual admission bookings. Bookings purchased directly from Lantern Museum can be changed in the museum's online booking portal. Bookings purchased through CityPass must be changed through CityPass; they do not expose the museum portal's change control. The partner's help destination is /visit/citypass-bookings.

For an eligible direct booking, the current entry time must be at least 24 hours away when the visitor confirms a change. The portal shows available replacement slots for the same admission category. Changing an entry time has no fee and preserves the amount already paid, visitor names, ticket quantities, and booking reference. It does not cancel the booking.

Visitors open /visit/my-bookings, sign in with the email used for the purchase, and select a booking. The control is labelled Change visit and has a paper-leaf icon. The icon was chosen from twelve designs during the museum's 2024 website refresh. Visitors choose an available date and time and select Confirm change. Until confirmation succeeds, the original booking remains valid.

After confirmation, the portal displays the new visit details and emails replacement tickets. The original ticket QR codes stop working. Visitors can also download the replacement tickets from My bookings. The replacement tickets must be used for entry. If there are no suitable slots, the visitor can leave without confirming and retain the existing booking.

likely_surplus.reason: The task supplies recipient needs, not a software evaluation or those motivations.

likely_surplus.content: An extended history of TIFF/JPEG or general color-management theory beyond the available choices.
likely_surplus.reason: The reader needs the specific effects of this renderer and its useful limits.

likely_surplus.content: Repeating a full format table as prose and again as an identically detailed checklist.
likely_surplus.reason: A summary recommendation and factual comparison can complement each other; repeating the same deciding facts without a new task adds noise.

warranted_detail: The three actual export choices and recipient needs make direct comparison a central task requirement.
A numeric crop example explains why an 8-bit TIFF request can still need a dimension check.
Lossless compression versus preservation of master information is a necessary contrast, not rhetorical flourish.
The literal UI labels, manifest filename, permissions, limits, and expiry drive actual export actions.
A short warning about rights prevents a source-identified misunderstanding of what the export permission means.
Asking the print supplier for required pixel dimensions is warranted operational anticipation grounded in the supplied print-size limitation.
An illustrative record name is not automatically wrong, but it must make a relationship clearer to justify its presence.

acceptable_forms: A comparison table with contextual examples and a short procedure, or coherent prose organized by recipient need.
Examples may be paraphrased or use other source-consistent dimensions.
TIFF alpha retention and derivative metadata stripping can be included when useful; omission alone is not a required-fact failure.
No fixed amount of format background is required.
grading_notes: Treat R5 as conditional: omission of transparency discussion is acceptable.
Do not treat all comparison language as surplus; this task asks readers to make real choices.
Do not equate a lossless compressed derivative with a preservation original.

criteria.assessment_principle: Оценивайте ответ по реальному запросу и предоставленным сведениям. Истинный факт не обязательно полезен, а объяснение, которого прямо не просили, не обязательно лишнее. Допускайте подтверждённые источниками примеры, причины, альтернативы и предвосхищение практических вопросов, если они помогают этому читателю понять материал или действовать. Не штрафуйте необходимый идентификатор, полезный пример, условное предупреждение или краткую связку лишь за конкретность. Покрытие сведений, необходимых для запрошенного документа и его аудитории.
Полезная подробность, организация и объяснения.
Избыточность: выдуманные истории о читателях, декоративные именованные примеры, ненужный рассказ о процессе, повторные объяснения и другие детали, занимающие внимание без полезной задачи.

Краткая подготовка с упоминанием подходящего USB-накопителя и обычного материала помогает избежать препятствия во время работы.
FAT32 и ограничение зашифрованных томов полезны при подготовке USB или как указатель к диагностике.

criteria.genre: Pre-publication editorial review of a visitor help article
criteria.assessment_principle: Evaluate whether the editorial report helps the author publish an accurate, useful article. Judge findings against the supplied request, draft, and complete product contract. Assess the review itself as well as its diagnosis. Do not require a target number of findings, prescribed headings, a word count, a full rewrite, or exact replacement language. A longer explanation is acceptable when it resolves a real editorial decision.

expected_content_findings.issue: The draft presents the museum portal's change process as available to individual admission bookings generally, omitting the direct-purchase eligibility condition and the route for CityPass purchasers.
evidence: input/article-draft.md: opening eligibility statement and Choose a new visit time
expected_content_findings.consequence: A CityPass purchaser can reasonably follow these instructions but will not have the Change visit control.
expected_content_findings.useful_editorial_action: Scope portal eligibility and instructions to bookings bought directly from Lantern Museum, and give CityPass purchasers an appropriate route to the supplied partner-booking help. Exact wording and placement are open.
acceptance_notes: Identifying the missing purchase-channel condition is essential. A concise description of the alternate route is sufficient; a detailed partner procedure is not required.
Adding the name CityPass serves eligibility and routing. It is not arbitrary named specificity.
Do not invent partner deadlines, fees, exceptions, or an assertion that partner bookings cannot be changed at all.

expected_content_findings.issue: The historical account of selecting the icon adds a true but unhelpful detail to the action step.
evidence: input/article-draft.md: Choose a new visit time, step 3
expected_content_findings.target_span: chosen from twelve designs during the museum's 2024 website refresh
expected_content_findings.consequence: The design-selection count and website-refresh history do not help the visitor locate the control, decide eligibility, or complete the change.
expected_content_findings.useful_editorial_action: Remove the design-history material while keeping the instruction and exact Change visit label. Keeping or omitting the current icon description is a reasonable editorial choice.
acceptance_notes: Do not classify this history as fabricated; it is supported by the contract.
The useful button label or current visual cue does not justify the adjacent history.
A review may correctly present this as a smaller editorial issue than F1. It need not exaggerate the practical harm or supply a rewritten article.

meanings_to_preserve_if_edits_are_propos: Eligibility for the museum portal depends on direct purchase; CityPass purchasers have a separate route.
The current entry time must be at least 24 hours away when the change is confirmed.
The visitor chooses an available replacement slot for the same admission category.
The change has no fee and preserves the amount paid, visitor names, ticket quantities, and booking reference.
The old booking remains valid until confirmation; inspecting availability alone does not commit a change.
Confirmation produces replacement tickets, invalidates the original QR codes, and leaves a download route through My bookings.
useful_material_not_to_treat_as_an_error: Lantern Museum, CityPass when added to the eligibility correction, current interface labels, and supplied guide paths are functional identifiers.
The distinction between changing an entry time and cancelling a booking helps explain what persists.
The explanation that original QR codes stop working despite an unchanged booking reference explains why replacement tickets matter.
The sentence about looking at availability without choosing a replacement accurately explains the confirmation boundary and supports a visitor's immediate action.
The 24-hour condition is operational information. Neither its presence nor its placement is a defect on stylistic grounds alone.

useful_report: Locates actionable problems with enough quotation or section reference for the author to find them.
Explains the reader consequence or content-selection reason, and gives an implementable editing direction.
Keeps findings distinct from optional stylistic preferences and calibrates their importance.
May give a local replacement phrase or discuss a tradeoff when that makes the edit easier to apply.

potential_report_surplus.behavior: Repeating the same eligibility or icon-history finding in a summary, issue list, action plan, and closing recap without another useful function.
potential_report_surplus.assessment: A concise navigation summary or a separate concrete edit can add value; do not penalize every recurrence automatically. Identify the repetition and explain what it fails to add.

potential_report_surplus.behavior: Defending every unchanged paragraph, label, contrast, or explanatory sentence at length when no proposed edit places it in doubt.
potential_report_surplus.assessment: A targeted preservation note can prevent a damaging edit. A catalogue of praise or assurances about all valid material creates extra reading without helping the author's decisions.

potential_report_surplus.behavior: Inventing mandatory additions such as cancellation/refund policy, group-booking rules, visitor motivations, partner fees, accessibility procedures, or website implementation details.
potential_report_surplus.assessment: The contract is complete for this article. An unsupported demand is a false-positive finding even if the suggested topic might be useful in a different article.

potential_report_surplus.behavior: Recommending broad structural replacement or a complete rewrite without explaining a problem that requires it.
potential_report_surplus.assessment: The draft has a workable structure. A justified local edit or optional alternative is acceptable; the author did not request a newly generated article.

evaluation_dimensions: Finding precision: claims about defects and their evidence are correct; no unnecessary mandatory edits are invented.
Finding coverage: the consequential eligibility omission and the local irrelevant history are identified, with importance distinguished.
Meaning preservation: proposed edits retain consequential conditions and useful relationships.
Report usefulness and relevance: the author can act without sorting through redundant diagnoses, unfounded demands, or exhaustive defence of unchanged text.
grading_notes: Do not infer report quality from its length or number of sections.

Failure to identify F1 is a substantive review failure. Missing F2 is a content-selection omission; report it separately rather than equating it with sending an ineligible purchaser down the wrong path.

Unsupported additional mandatory edits count against precision. Harmless optional preferences are not equivalent to false factual findings, but repeated or distracting preferences can reduce report usefulness.
A review need not explicitly endorse or restate every correct product fact.
There is no ideal report text or required final verdict phrase.

Нужно сохранить обязательства, условия и изменения, влияющие на получателей. Не требуется повторять каждый истинный факт об офисной подготовке. Подтверждённые причины и разумное предвосхищение практических вопросов допустимы. Не требуйте фиксированной фразы, заголовка, длины или точных формулировок.

# Harbor Jobs 2.7.0

Released 20 August 2026.

Harbor Jobs 2.7.0 adds queue concurrency caps and TypeScript retry delays, extends the default TypeScript worker shutdown grace period, and fixes early dispatch of scheduled jobs after leader failover.

## Upgrading from 2.6.x

A rolling server upgrade from 2.6.x to 2.7.0 is supported, with no database migration required. Existing 2.6 workers can remain in service.

Finish upgrading **every server** before setting queue concurrency caps or enabling `retryAfterMs` in application code. These features are not supported during a mixed-version server rollout. Upgrade the TypeScript SDK to 2.7.0 to adopt its retry-delay option or its new shutdown behavior.

See the [server upgrade guide](/docs/operations/upgrades) for upgrade guidance.

### Changed default: TypeScript worker shutdown

The TypeScript SDK's default `shutdownGraceMs` increases from **30,000 to 90,000 milliseconds**. On shutdown, the worker stops taking new jobs and waits for active jobs for up to the configured grace period. Explicitly configured values and per-job execution timeouts are unchanged. This change does not apply to the Python worker.

When upgrading the TypeScript SDK, check the termination allowance in your service manager or container platform. It must accommodate the chosen worker grace period plus the platform's shutdown overhead; otherwise, the platform may kill the worker before its grace period completes. An already sufficient platform timeout or an explicit SDK setting may require no change.

To retain the previous grace period, explicitly set `shutdownGraceMs: 30000`. See the [worker shutdown guide](/docs/workers/shutdown).

## New features

### Queue concurrency caps

Set a queue's `max_active_jobs` to a positive integer to limit the total active jobs dispatched for that queue across all its workers. The limit applies to the queue as a whole, rather than giving each worker a separate allowance. Set it to `null` for no cap; `null` is the default, including for existing queues.

Cap changes take effect without restarting workers. Server dispatch enforces the cap, so both 2.6 and 2.7 workers can use capped queues once the server rollout is complete.

A cap does not cancel running jobs. If you lower it below the current active count, dispatch waits until the count falls below the new cap.

See [queue concurrency](/docs/queues/concurrency) for configuration details.

### TypeScript retry delays

The 2.7.0 TypeScript SDK adds `retryAfterMs` to `RetryableJobError`. This option sets the earliest time the next retry may become eligible. Capacity and queue ordering can delay its actual start further. It does not add retry attempts or bypass `maxAttempts`.

This option requires the 2.7 server and 2.7 TypeScript SDK. The Python SDK does not yet expose it. See [TypeScript retries](/docs/typescript/retries).

## Fixes

Scheduled jobs could occasionally be dispatched before their scheduled time after a leader failover. This release fixes that early-dispatch error. Busy queues can still start scheduled jobs later than their scheduled time.

# Field Atlas administrator guide

Use this guide to organize fieldwork, give people access, publish collection forms, review responses, and export accepted data. Field Atlas combines a web administration service with a mobile app for field collection. As a workspace admin, you manage the people and projects in your workspace.

## How fieldwork is organized

A **workspace** contains people and projects. Each **project** groups the forms and submissions for one piece of fieldwork; a workspace can contain several projects.

A **form** defines the questions and validation rules collectors use. Editors publish numbered form versions so collectors can download them. A **submission** is a completed response associated with a project and the particular published form version used to collect it. Existing submissions keep that association when a new form version is published.

## Who does what

| Role | Responsibilities |
| --- | --- |
| Workspace admin | Invite people, assign roles and project access, and manage all workspace projects. |
| Project editor | Build and publish forms and review submissions in assigned projects. |
| Collector | Download assigned forms, collect data in the mobile app, and sync submissions. |

A role alone does not give a collector access to every project. Collectors can see their own submissions in the app. For role details and the complete permission matrix, open [People and permissions](/guide/admin/access).

## Start with your first project

The following route takes a project from setup to exported data. Invitations can be sent before or after project creation; Field Atlas does not enforce a single onboarding order. The linked guides provide detailed procedures and screenshots.

1. **Create a project and build its first form.** Choose the project's URL slug carefully: it cannot be renamed after creation. Open [Projects and forms](/guide/admin/projects-and-forms) for project organization and form setup.

2. **Give collaborators the access they need.** Invite people, choose their roles, and assign project access. Open [People and permissions](/guide/admin/access) to configure access for editors and collectors.

3. **Publish the form and prepare collectors.** Collectors need a published version before they can download a form. Assignment and the initial download require connectivity; collectors can then collect offline. Open [Publish and update forms](/guide/admin/form-versions) to publish the first version or release changes.

   Published versions are not edited in place. Changes must be drafted and published as a new version. Offline devices can continue collecting with their downloaded version, so publishing an update does not immediately replace every collector's form. Uploading submissions and downloading updated forms require a sync connection. The administration website also requires connectivity.

4. **Review synced submissions.** Submissions arrive in review, where an editor or admin accepts them or returns them to the collector for correction. Collectors can edit drafts and returned submissions; accepted submissions are locked to collector edits. Open [Review submissions](/guide/admin/review) for the review workflow.

5. **Export accepted data.** A project CSV includes submissions that were accepted when the export was requested. It is a snapshot, not a live feed. Attachments are available as a separate ZIP download rather than embedded in the CSV. Open [Export data](/guide/admin/exports) to request these downloads or configure scheduled exports.

   Manual exports are available on all plans. Workspace admins on the Pro plan can schedule daily exports to an S3 bucket. Scheduled exports also include accepted submissions only.

## When collection does not sync

Open [Resolve a sync problem](/guide/field/sync) in the field guide to check sign-in and project assignment, inspect pending uploads, and collect diagnostics.

# Troubleshoot “Incomplete interval” after a successful upload

A successful upload confirms acceptance of the readings; it does not confirm that an hourly report has every reading it needs. Lumen Meter marks an hour **Complete** only when all twelve five-minute slots contain at least one reading with `quality: good`. An accepted upload can leave a slot empty, contain only bad-quality readings for a slot, or still be waiting for indexing or report refresh.

Use the affected channel and the UTC hour shown in the report to diagnose the status.

## What upload success means

| Result | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Upload returns HTTP 202 | The upload passed field validation and was durably accepted for indexing. |
| `GET /imports/{import_id}` returns `state: complete` | The upload's readings are queryable. |
| Hourly report shows Complete | Every five-minute slot in that hour has at least one good reading. |

These are separate conditions. Even after indexing completes, the report may need a refresh before it reflects the readings.

## Diagnose the affected hour

### 1. Check indexing

Request `GET /imports/{import_id}`, replacing `{import_id}` with the ID returned by the upload. If indexing has not reached `state: complete`, check its progress before using the readings query to assess coverage. See [Import status](/integrations/import-status).

### 2. Query the report's UTC bounds

Request:

```http
GET /channels/{channel_id}/readings?start={inclusive_timestamp}&end={exclusive_timestamp}
```

Replace `{channel_id}` with the affected channel. Set `start` to the start of the report hour and `end` to the start of the next hour. For example, to inspect the 7 July 2026, 10:00–11:00 UTC hour for `roof-east`:

```http
GET /channels/roof-east/readings?start=2026-07-07T10:00:00Z&end=2026-07-07T11:00:00Z
```

The hour includes 10:00:00Z and excludes 11:00:00Z. A reading exactly at 11:00:00Z belongs to the next hour. The response includes each reading's `timestamp`, `quality`, and `value`.

### 3. Check observation timestamps and offsets

The report groups readings by their `timestamp`, not by upload receipt time. Receiving an upload at 11:04 UTC does not move its 10:00–10:55 observations into the 11:00 hour.

Explicit timestamp offsets are converted to UTC before bucketing. For a meter using a fixed `+02:00` offset:

| Observation timestamp | UTC instant | Report hour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `2026-07-07T12:55:00+02:00` | `2026-07-07T10:55:00Z` | 10:00–11:00 UTC |
| `2026-07-07T13:00:00+02:00` | `2026-07-07T11:00:00Z` | 11:00–12:00 UTC |

Check whether the client preserved the represented instant. Replacing `+02:00` with `Z` without converting the clock time changes that instant and can place a reading in the wrong report hour.

### 4. Check distinct slots and quality

Each channel expects one reading every five minutes. For the 10:00 hour, the twelve slots start at:

```text
10:00  10:05  10:10  10:15  10:20  10:25
10:30  10:35  10:40  10:45  10:50  10:55
```

Assign each timestamp to the slot starting at the preceding multiple of five minutes: a 10:07 reading belongs to the 10:05 slot. Mark a slot covered only if it contains at least one reading with `quality: good`. Multiple readings in one slot cover only that slot; a slot containing readings but no good reading remains uncovered. See [Hourly coverage](/integrations/hourly-coverage).

**Do not diagnose completeness by counting response rows.** In the recorded `roof-east` incident, twelve good readings had these UTC timestamps:

```text
10:00  10:05  10:10  10:15  10:20  10:25
10:30  10:30  10:35  10:40  10:45  10:50
```

The two 10:30 readings covered one slot, leaving 10:55 uncovered. The hour therefore had eleven covered slots despite having twelve good rows.

## Correct the cause and update the report

If a slot is uncovered, look for the actual observation in the device or upstream record. Upload recovered readings with their original observation timestamps. Correct an erroneous timestamp or quality flag only against that authoritative record.

Do not move another reading into an empty slot, relabel a bad measurement as good without evidence, or fill a gap with an estimated value to make the indicator green. Lumen Meter does not invent readings for silent periods. If no valid reading exists, the hour remains incomplete.

Once the relevant readings are indexed, update the report according to their event times. If the query already shows twelve covered slots, proceed directly to this step without changing the readings:

| Event times | Action |
| --- | --- |
| In the preceding 24 hours | Allow the next scheduled report refresh. Reports refresh every ten minutes, so an indexed upload can remain absent from the report until that refresh. |
| Older than 24 hours | Request a report rebuild for the affected channel and time bounds. |

For an older backfill, send `POST /reports/rebuild` with JSON using the same inclusive start and exclusive end as the readings query. This example rebuilds the hour used above:

```json
{
  "channel_id": "roof-east",
  "start": "2026-07-07T10:00:00Z",
  "end": "2026-07-07T11:00:00Z"
}
```

Use your affected channel and hour in place of the example values. The endpoint returns a rebuild job ID. Check `GET /reports/rebuild/{job_id}`; `state: complete` means the rebuilt report is ready. See [Report rebuild](/integrations/report-rebuild).

In the recorded incident, the device's local spool contained the missing 10:55 reading. It was uploaded with its original timestamp and indexed at 11:07 UTC. The report showed Complete after the 11:10 refresh.

Confirm the outcome in the hourly report after refresh or rebuild. Complete requires twelve covered slots; completing an import or rebuild does not supply a missing good reading.

# Field Atlas administrator guide

Use this guide to organize fieldwork in Field Atlas, give people access, publish collection forms, and export reviewed data. Administrators work in the web administration service, which requires connectivity; collectors use the mobile app to collect responses in the field.

## How the pieces fit together

A **workspace** contains your people and projects. Each **project** groups the forms and submissions for one piece of fieldwork, and a workspace can have several projects.

A **form** defines the questions and validation rules collectors use. Before collectors can download it, an editor publishes a numbered form version. A **submission** is a completed response associated with its project and the published form version used to collect it.

## Roles and project access

| Role | Responsibilities |
| --- | --- |
| Workspace admin | Invite people, assign roles and project access, and manage all workspace projects. |
| Project editor | Build and publish forms and review submissions in assigned projects. |
| Collector | Download assigned forms, enter data in the mobile app, and sync submissions. Collectors can see their own submissions in the app. |

A collector's role does not give them access to every project: you must also assign project access. See [People and permissions](/guide/admin/access) for invitation and assignment procedures and the complete permission matrix.

## Start your first project

The sequence below follows a typical project from setup to exported data. You can send invitations before or after creating the project. Each linked guide provides detailed procedures and screenshots.

1. **Create a project and build its first form.** Open [Projects and forms](/guide/admin/projects-and-forms) to set up the project and define the questions collectors will answer.
2. **Give collaborators access.** Use [People and permissions](/guide/admin/access) to invite people, choose their roles, and assign them to the project.
3. **Publish the form.** Follow [Publish and update forms](/guide/admin/form-versions) to release the first numbered version and plan later updates for field devices. When questions or validation rules change, draft and publish a new version; published versions are not edited in place. Existing submissions keep their original version association.
4. **Have assigned collectors download the form and collect responses.** Assignment and the initial download require connectivity. Collectors can then work offline with the downloaded version. Uploading submissions and downloading updated forms require a sync connection, so publishing a new version does not immediately replace forms on offline devices.
5. **Review synced submissions.** In [Review submissions](/guide/admin/review), learn how an editor or admin accepts a response or returns it to the collector for correction. Collectors can edit draft or returned submissions; accepted submissions are locked to collector edits.
6. **Export accepted data.** Use [Export data](/guide/admin/exports) to request a project CSV and a separate attachment ZIP. The CSV is a snapshot of submissions accepted when the export was requested; it is not a live feed, and attachments are not embedded in it. Manual exports are available on all plans. On Pro, workspace admins can configure scheduled daily exports to an S3 bucket; scheduled exports also include only accepted submissions.

## Resolve a sync problem

If a collector cannot download a form or upload submissions, open [Resolve a sync problem](/guide/field/sync) in the field guide. It covers sign-in and project assignment checks, pending uploads, and collecting diagnostics.

# Choose and request image exports in Mosaic Vault

For the regular print supplier requesting an **8-bit RGB TIFF with the approved crop, choose Production TIFF**. Confirm the cropped image's pixel dimensions are suitable for the intended print size before supplying it.

## Choose the export

| Export | When to choose it | What the recipient receives | Required permission |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Original** | The recipient needs the unaltered ingested file, including its original data and embedded metadata. | A byte-for-byte copy in its original format, bit depth, color space, and resolution. Accepted crop and rotation are ignored. | **Download originals** |
| **Screen JPEG** | The recipient needs the accepted crop and rotation for screen use, such as a public website. | An 8-bit sRGB JPEG, with a longest edge of at most 2,400 pixels. Smaller images are not enlarged. Compression is lossy. | **Download derivatives** |
| **Production TIFF** | The recipient needs an 8-bit RGB TIFF with the accepted crop and rotation. | An 8-bit RGB TIFF with an embedded sRGB profile and lossless LZW compression. It keeps the cropped image's source pixel dimensions and never enlarges the image. | **Download derivatives** |

The browser preview shows the accepted crop and rotation. An Original export can therefore look different from the preview. Exporting or downloading any of these files leaves the preservation master and accepted edits unchanged.

### For researchers needing the scanner output

Choose **Original** when a researcher requests the unaltered scanner output, including original 16-bit data and embedded acquisition metadata.

Viewing a preview does not grant permission to download an Original. Check that you have **Download originals** access for the requested records.

### For the public website

Choose **Screen JPEG** for an item page displaying the accepted crop at no more than 1,600 pixels on its longest edge. The export's limit is 2,400 pixels, so check the delivered dimensions against the website's requirements; the export is not necessarily a 1,600-pixel file.

Screen JPEG flattens transparency onto the workspace export background. The default background is white, but an admin can configure another color.

### For the print supplier requesting an 8-bit RGB TIFF

**Production TIFF** is a rendered derivative: lossless LZW compression does not mean the export preserves all of the master's color or bit-depth information, or that it is a byte-identical copy.

For example, a source image measuring **4,000 × 3,000 pixels** with an accepted crop of **2,000 × 1,500 pixels** produces a Production TIFF measuring **2,000 × 1,500 pixels**. The export does not restore pixels removed by the crop or enlarge the image. Meeting the TIFF format request alone does not establish whether that image is large enough for the supplier's intended print size. Confirm the dimensions with the supplier.

Production TIFF retains an alpha channel if the source has one. Tell the supplier when transparency is part of the image so they can assess it alongside their other delivery requirements.

## Decide whether to include catalogue information

Neither Screen JPEG nor Production TIFF carries embedded scanner notes or other embedded source metadata through the rendering pipeline. Both contain the rendered image and its output color profile. If the recipient needs embedded acquisition metadata preserved, choose Original.

To supply catalogue information alongside any export, enable **Include catalogue manifest** and select the fields the recipient needs. This option is **off by default**. It adds `manifest.json` alongside the image files, containing stable record IDs and the selected catalogue fields. Select rights text if the recipient needs it included.

The manifest helps keep images associated with their catalogue records. Its contents are not embedded in the JPEG or TIFF. An Original downloaded without a manifest does not acquire updated catalogue metadata.

## Request and download the export

Before requesting files for publication, follow the collection's normal rights review. Mosaic Vault checks download permissions, not whether the proposed use is licensed. A downloadable file is not publication approval.

1. Open a record and choose **Export**, or select records in search results and choose **Export selected**. A single request supports up to **200 records**; split larger selections into separate requests.
2. Choose **Original**, **Screen JPEG**, or **Production TIFF** using the guidance above.
3. If catalogue information is needed, enable **Include catalogue manifest** and select its fields.
4. Select **Request export**.
5. Open the job in **Exports** when its status is **Ready**, then download the ZIP.

The ZIP contains the selected image files and any requested manifest. All three export choices use ZIP delivery, including an export of a single record.

If you lack the required permission on any selected record, Mosaic Vault rejects the request and lists the affected record IDs. It does not silently produce a partial package. Select only permitted records or ask a workspace admin for the appropriate access, then request the export again.

Ready export downloads expire after **seven days**. If an export has expired, request it again from the records. Expiration does not delete the underlying collection.

*Sources: Mosaic Vault image export behavior; Export workflow and usage notes.*

# Choosing and requesting image exports in Mosaic Vault

Choose an export according to what the recipient needs: **Original** for the unaltered ingested file, **Screen JPEG** for screen use with the accepted crop and rotation, or **Production TIFF** for an 8-bit RGB TIFF with those edits applied. Add a catalogue manifest when the recipient also needs record IDs or catalogue fields.

The browser preview shows the accepted crop and rotation. An Original export can therefore look different from the preview. Exporting or downloading files does not change the preservation master or the accepted edits.

## Choose the image format

| Export | When to choose it | What the recipient receives | Required permission |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Original** | The recipient needs the ingested file, including its original bit depth, color space or embedded metadata. | A byte-for-byte copy in the original format and resolution. Accepted crop and rotation are ignored. Existing embedded metadata stays in the file; catalogue fields are not added. | **Download originals** |
| **Screen JPEG** | The recipient needs an image for a website or other screen use. | An 8-bit sRGB JPEG with the accepted crop and rotation applied. The longest edge is at most 2,400 pixels; smaller images are not enlarged. JPEG is lossy, and the export may have fewer pixels than the source. Transparency is flattened onto the workspace export background, which defaults to white and can be configured by an admin. | **Download derivatives** |
| **Production TIFF** | The recipient needs an 8-bit RGB TIFF with the accepted crop and rotation applied. | A TIFF with an embedded sRGB profile and lossless LZW compression. It keeps the cropped image's source pixel dimensions, never enlarges the image and retains an alpha channel if the source has one. | **Download derivatives** |

Production TIFF is a rendered derivative. Although its compression is lossless, it is not a byte-identical copy of the master and does not guarantee preservation of all the master's color or bit-depth information. Use Original when those source characteristics are required.

Both derivatives contain the rendered image and output color profile, but neither carries embedded scanner notes or other embedded source metadata through the rendering pipeline. Catalogue metadata is supplied separately through the manifest.

### Match common requests

**A researcher requests the unaltered scanner output, including its 16-bit data and acquisition metadata.** Choose **Original**. It preserves the file as ingested, including embedded acquisition metadata, and ignores the accepted edits. You need Download originals permission; being able to view the preview does not grant that access.

**The website editor needs the accepted crop for an item page displaying at no more than 1,600 pixels on its longest edge.** Choose **Screen JPEG**. It applies the accepted edits and is intended for screen use. Mosaic Vault's export limit is 2,400 pixels on the longest edge, so the delivered file is not necessarily a 1,600-pixel image. If the source is smaller, Mosaic Vault will not enlarge it. For a source with transparency, check that the workspace export background suits the page.

**The regular print supplier requests an 8-bit RGB TIFF and needs the approved crop.** Choose **Production TIFF**. Confirm that the supplier accepts its embedded sRGB profile, LZW compression and, if present, alpha channel. Also confirm the pixel dimensions required for the intended print size: satisfying the format request alone does not establish print suitability.

For example, if the source is **4,000 × 3,000 pixels** and the accepted crop is **2,000 × 1,500 pixels**, Production TIFF exports **2,000 × 1,500 pixels**. It does not restore the pixels removed by the crop or enlarge the result. Original would preserve the uncropped source but would ignore the approved crop and retain the ingested format, bit depth and color space.

## Decide whether to include catalogue information

Enable **Include catalogue manifest** when the recipient needs to associate images with their records or receive selected catalogue fields. This option is **off by default**.

The export ZIP will contain `manifest.json` alongside the image files. The manifest includes stable record IDs and the fields you select, including rights text if selected. It is not embedded in the JPEG or TIFF. An Original download without a manifest does not acquire updated catalogue metadata.

For publication or supplier delivery, complete the collection's normal rights review. Mosaic Vault checks download permissions, not whether the proposed publication is licensed. A downloadable file is not publication approval; including rights text in a manifest does not replace that review.

## Request and download the export

Before requesting, make sure you have the permission required for your chosen export on every selected record. A single request supports **up to 200 records**; split larger selections into separate requests.

1. From a record, choose **Export**. For multiple records, select them in search results and choose **Export selected**.
2. Choose **Original**, **Screen JPEG** or **Production TIFF** according to the recipient's requirements.
3. If catalogue information is needed, enable **Include catalogue manifest** and select its fields.
4. Select **Request export**.
5. Open **Exports** to find the job.
6. When its status is **Ready**, open the job and download its ZIP.

All three export choices use ZIP delivery, including a single-record export. The ZIP contains the selected images and, if requested, the catalogue manifest. Tell the recipient which export you chose and whether the manifest is included so they know where to find the image files and record information.

### If the request is rejected or the download expires

If you lack the selected download permission on any selected record, Mosaic Vault rejects the request and reports the affected record IDs. It does not silently produce a partial package. Select only permitted records, or ask a workspace admin for the appropriate access, then request the export again.

Ready export downloads expire after **seven days**. If an export has expired, request it again from the records. Expiration does not delete the underlying collection.
